transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-26 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Ana (Redwood Product), Ethan (Skyline CTO), Priya (Skyline ML), Marcus (Skyline Infra)

Summary:
Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and quality vs latency tradeoffs for Skyline AI's real-time summarization use case. Discussed benchmark methodology, representative prompt sets, expected latency improvements with INT8 and FP8, fallback and routing policies, and security considerations for Dedicated/Private deployments. Agreed next steps: share quantization spreadsheet, security docs, and schedule a 2-week pilot with benchmark runs.

Topics:
- Quantization profiles: INT8, FP8, hybrid profiles
- Quality vs latency: expected delta and how we measure it
- Benchmarks: throughput, p95/p99 latencies, token-level costs
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS)
- Eval methodology: prompt sets, BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and human spot checks

Action items (brief): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, we, um, we have about 45 minutes, we'll run through Optimize quant profiles and then leave time for questions. Ethan you mentioned you, uh, sent over some example prompts earlier, is that right?
[00:08] Ethan: Yeah, sent them last night, you should have a bucket link, maybe there was a permission thing, Priya will re-share after.
[00:13] Maya: Great, perfect. Leo do you want to kick off with the slides?
[00:16] Leo: Yep, I'll share. Hi all, I'm Leo, I'm the SE on this. Quick agenda: what quant profiles are, why INT8/FP8 matter, our quality vs latency matrix, then a demo of Optimize recommending profiles for your workload.
[00:28] Priya: Quick note - our production SLO is p95 inference < 250ms for short summarize requests (~80 tokens) and average payload is 60 tokens. That's our bar.
[00:36] Leo: Great that's helpful. So quantization - short version - reduces model weights precision to trade compute for memory and faster kernels. INT8 typically gives largest perf win, FP8 gives intermediate speed up with often better quality retention vs INT8. We also support mixed profiles, e.g., activations FP8, weights INT8 - the profiles we show later.
[00:58] Ethan: Do you have real numbers? Like if we move from FP16 to INT8 what kind of latency improvement can we expect?
[01:05] Leo: Good question. For the base Llama-ish 7B variants on A100-ish class, from FP16 to INT8 we often see 30-50% CPU/GPU utilization reduction and token latency drops around 20-40% depending on sequence length and batch. FP8 usually sits in the 10-25% latency improvement range with smaller quality drop. But that's model and prompt dependent.
[01:30] Marcus: Our infra is GCP with T4s in prod, we're sensitive to memory footprints. Does Redwood Optimize suggest profiles per model and hardware?
[01:38] Ana: Yes - Optimize profiles are hardware-aware. It looks at your sequence length distribution, KV cache patterns, and suggests profiles that optimize for latency or throughput depending on your SLOs.
[01:47] [01:47] Leo: I'm pulling up a sample Optimize run - forgive the perf dash noise, it's internal.
[01:52] Leo: Example: Skyline-like workload (short chatty summaries), we ran three profiles: FP16 (baseline), FP8, INT8. For p95 latency: FP16 310ms, FP8 250ms, INT8 195ms (on N4x T4-equivalent). Quality (we did automated BLEU-ish + human micro-eval) showed FP8 ~99% of baseline, INT8 ~92-95% depending on prompt complexity.
[02:20] Priya: That p95 number for FP16 is higher than our target; our current infra is tuned, but those numbers help.
[02:25] Leo: Right - these were single-instance runs without aggressive batching. With Redwood's batching you'll see different throughput-latency tradeoffs; Optimize can recommend batch sizes too.
[02:33] Ethan: What about hallucinations or subtle quality regressions - can you show examples where INT8 fails?
[02:38] Leo: Yes, we included adversarial prompts in the eval set. Typical failure modes: rare token probabilities shift so you might get slightly altered named entities or punctuation issues in long-form. For summarization we saw occasional missing clause or slightly compressed paraphrase - humans flagged about 8% of INT8 outputs in a small set while FP8 had 1-2%.
[02:58] [02:58] Speaker 1: hmm
[03:00] Marcus: From a cost perspective, what's the delta? If INT8 reduces GPU utilization how maps to cost savings on Redwood Dedicated?
[03:07] Ana: Cost depends on reserved vs burst and model selection. Ballpark: INT8 can reduce per-token GPU cost by ~25-40% after you factor in higher throughput, but if quality regressions are unacceptable you'll stay FP8 or FP16. Optimize shows per-token cost estimates alongside quality metrics in the console.
[03:24] Maya: Also worth noting caching - if you have heavy prefix reuse our KV cache reduces tokens that need compute, changing the economics. Did you mention your prompt distribution earlier, Priya?
[03:34] Priya: Yeah majority are short prompts with common prefixes, about 35% prefix reuse across users.
[03:39] Leo: Then caching will help, and we might lean more aggressive to INT8 for tail traffic - Optimize can recommend routing policies: e.g., route 80% to FP8 and 20% to INT8 for non-critical queries.
[03:52] Ethan: How do you validate via our evals - do you run our prompts directly?
[03:56] Leo: We prefer you provide a representative set (Priya's 500 prompts would be perfect). We'll run them across each profile and collect metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, automated ngram metrics, and a small human spot check. We also do diff scoring relative to a chosen baseline.
[04:13] Priya: Can you ingest our internal labels? Like we have importance-weighted queries where some must be high-quality.
[04:18] Ana: Yep Optimize supports weighting prompts so the profiler optimizes for the weighted metric \u2014 that lets you bias towards quality for critical prompts and cost for others.
[04:25] [04:25] Leo: Next, demo of the Console - I'll switch screens to the Optimize tab.
[04:32] Leo: (screen share) Here is the profile explorer - each line is a profile: quant strategy, expected latency, quality delta, cost estimate. You can filter by hardware family, model, or by SLO target.
[04:42] Maya: Note - sometimes transcript picks up model names wrong, we call them Llama-2 but sometimes it's spelled Lama or LAMA in exports, ignore that.
[04:49] Ethan: On the console can you do live A/B? Like send 10% traffic to INT8 and 90% to FP8?
[04:54] Leo: Yes we support canary and traffic splitting natively. You can define rollout policies, automatic rollback on regressions, and metric windows.
[05:02] Marcus: Security - if we do Dedicated in our VPC will logs ever leave our environment? We have strict CR requirements.
[05:08] Maya: For Private we support customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integration; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and we can obfuscate PII. For Dedicated the control plane is Redwood but you can choose that logs don't contain raw customer data. We'll share the security deck.
[05:22] Ethan: Is SOC2 in place? Also compliance for EU data residency?
[05:25] Maya: Yes SOC2 Type II, we have regional deployments and can run Private in a customer VPC for residency. I'll attach the SOC2 summary.
[05:34] Priya: Back to quant — are there model architectures that just don't work with INT8 well?
[05:38] Leo: Some newer attention variants or very small models with fused kernels can be fragile. Also quantization-aware training helps; for off-the-shelf large models we rely on per-layer calibration and some post-training quant techniques. FP8 is often a safer middle ground.
[05:52] [05:52] Ethan: For our roadmap, we may prioritize cost first then roll quality tests. We'd like a pilot to see real metrics on our data.
[05:58] Maya: Totally, piloting with your prompts is the normal next step. We'll provision a dedicated bench harness and run the three profiles.
[06:05] Leo: Quick note on benchmarks - we recommend multiple seeds and realistic warm cache conditions. Cold-starts with KV cache empty can look worse; we simulate your traffic pattern though.
[06:16] Priya: Will Redwood run micro-evals or do we need to do human review?
[06:19] Leo: We'll run automated evals and a small human review pack; for production you typically run an initial human review then automate. We can include Skyline engineers in the review loop.
[06:28] Ethan: On the cost estimate, is it only GPU hour math or includes networking, storage?
[06:32] Ana: The per-token cost estimate focuses on compute & amortized infra; we include storage impacts when relevant (e.g., large KV caches), but network egress is separate line item in the pricing sheet.
[06:42] [06:42] Speaker 2: mm-hmm
[06:44] Marcus: If we go INT8 and see 8% degradation for certain prompts, can we route only those prompts to FP8 automatically?
[06:50] Leo: Yes - Optimize can create route rules using prompt classifiers or metadata flags. For example, tag critical prompts with priority=high and route to FP8, lower priority to INT8.
[07:01] Priya: Will that add complexity to our codebase?
[07:04] Maya: Minimal, you can set per-route config in API calls or in Console, no code change if you use header-based routing.
[07:10] Ethan: Can we test a hybrid approach - weights INT8 but activations FP8 - does Optimize recommend that?
[07:15] Leo: We do. Hybrid profiles are common for balancing quality vs perf. The profiler will evaluate hybrid and purely INT8/FP8. Often hybrid hits sweet spot: 15-30% latency drop with quality near FP16.
[07:27] [07:27] Priya: Any gotchas with batching? We use small batch sizes because of latency SLOs.
[07:31] Leo: Batching increases throughput but can increase tail latency - Optimize models per-batch latency curve and suggests batch sizes that meet your p95 SLO. For small batch SLOs it's more about kernel-level perf and memory fit.
[07:43] Marcus: For our T4 fleet, is INT8 supported in your runtime or do we need specific libs?
[07:48] Leo: Redwood runtime supports INT8/FP8 on both Ampere and Turing families with our kernel stack; we select kernels per hardware. No infra change needed from your side besides enabling profile in deployment config.
[07:59] Ethan: How do we monitor model regressions once in prod?
[08:02] Ana: Console has continuous quality monitoring - you can register prompt sets and golden outputs; we sample outputs, score diffs, and trigger alerts if drift/regression thresholds exceeded.
[08:12] Priya: Nice. On the crawl - do you keep raw outputs for debugging?
[08:16] Maya: We can store outputs in customer-controlled storage for Private. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide redacted logs by default and can enable raw output retention with appropriate controls in contract.
[08:27] Leo: Demo time - here's an Optimize run for a Skyline-like set.
[08:31] [08:31] Leo: (shows table) Profile A: FP16 baseline - p95 310ms, quality index 100%, cost X. Profile B: FP8 - p95 250ms, quality 99%, cost X * 0.85. Profile C: INT8 - p95 195ms, quality 93%, cost X * 0.6.
[08:47] Priya: For summary use case quality index 93% may be too low, but for ephemeral chat suggestions could be fine.
[08:54] Leo: Exactly the trade. You can do route splits by intent too.
[08:58] Ethan: Can Optimize output include worst-case example outputs so we know what to expect?
[09:02] Leo: Yes - we include diff examples - like the INT8 failure we saw here where a date token was truncated and a name spelled wrong. We attach side-by-side comparisons in the results.
[09:12] [09:12] Speaker 1: uh huh
[09:13] Marcus: How long does a pilot typically take?
[09:16] Maya: Usually 2 weeks to run benchmarks and human review. Then we reconvene to pick final profile and rollout strategy.
[09:22] Ethan: Ok let's tentatively book that.
[09:24] Priya: One more question - do you support custom quantization profiles (we trained a quant-aware model)?
[09:30] Leo: Yes, you can bring quant-aware trained weights. We also support custom kernels if needed; our runtime can ingest model artifacts and we run calibration hooks. There can be extra engineering time for non-standard graph ops.
[09:43] Ana: Also note that model upgrades and versioning are first-class in Console - you can pin a version and run rollouts.
[09:49] [09:49] Ethan: Regarding SLOs, can Optimize recommend profiles to hit a target p95 < 250ms?
[09:55] Leo: Yes - you set SLO and Optimize will filter profiles that meet it and rank by cost and quality. For your SLO of 250ms p95, FP8 looks promising based on our initial sim.
[10:06] Marcus: Any network impact from switching profiles?
[10:09] Ana: Not really - it's compute-bound mostly. But if you reduce payloads or compress tokens differently networking could be slightly different.
[10:16] Priya: If we do Dedicated, what is the provisioning lead time?
[10:20] Maya: Dependent on commit; can be days for small bench setups, weeks for full reserved pools. We'll share standard timelines.
[10:28] [10:28] Leo: Quick pause for Qs from Skyline - anything else on quant?
[10:32] Priya: How do you handle tokenizer mismatches between our pipeline and models?
[10:35] Leo: We recommend standardizing tokenizer at ingestion; Optimize accounts for tokenizer differences during evaluation; sometimes minor tokenization differences can change quality metrics, we flag them.
[10:44] Ethan: On the human evals, what's sample size?
[10:47] Leo: Typical is 200-500 samples with stratified sampling across prompt types; for critical flows we do larger.
[10:54] [10:54] Speaker 1: okay
[10:56] Marcus: Pricing - can we get per-token delta estimates transformed into expected monthly bill for our traffic?
[11:01] Ana: Yes if you share traffic profile we can project monthly costs by profile. That's part of the pilot output.
[11:08] Priya: Any risk of model divergence if we use mixed profiles?
[11:12] Leo: No divergence in model semantics beyond stochasticity; mixed profiles means different numeric precision but runtime ensures deterministic seeds for fair comparison. We do see small variance in rare cases.
[11:23] Ethan: We need to involve legal/security folks early - will you share the compliance artifacts?
[11:27] Maya: Yes I'll send SOC2, encryption and data flow diagrams, and the contract checklist.
[11:34] [11:34] Maya: Okay let's do a quick live example \u2014 I'm going to ask Optimize: recommend profile for Skyline SLO p95 < 250ms, weight critical prompts 0.7.
[11:44] Leo: (types) Running profile search... results in 2-3 minutes usually - but here's cached run: top pick FP8 hybrid with activation FP8 & weights INT8 at medium calibration gives p95 235ms quality 99% cost 0.82X.
[11:58] Priya: That looks promising.
[12:00] Ethan: If we want to further reduce cost, what's the next step?
[12:03] Leo: Try asymmetric routing - route non-critical to INT8; or use more aggressive quant with augmentation like temperature scaling to reduce hallucination risk.
[12:13] Marcus: Any new hardware support coming that changes this calculus?
[12:16] Ana: Yes upcoming GPU generations with native FP8/INT8 kernels can shift savings; Optimize periodically re-profiles for new hardware.
[12:25] [12:25] Ethan: Are there cases where FP8 is strictly better than INT8 across both quality and latency?
[12:30] Leo: Sometimes FP8 hits a sweet spot on certain models quant noise pattern is lower so FP8 has near baseline quality and good latency; INT8 still best for raw memory-constrained throughput.
[12:42] Priya: For the pilot can we include an A/B with live user traffic or just synthetic?
[12:46] Maya: Both. We can do shadow testing on live traffic then roll traffic percentages gradually. Shadow testing is useful before human review.
[12:54] [12:54] Speaker 2: right
[12:56] Ethan: Okay that covers the technical questions I think.
[12:59] Maya: Great, recap of next steps: Priya provide prompts/traffic profile by 2026-03-29; Leo will run Optimize and share quant spreadsheet by 2026-03-30; Maya to send security & pricing docs by 2026-03-30; schedule pilot to start week of 2026-04-06. Anything else?
[13:18] Priya: No, thanks. Marcus: No.
[13:21] Ethan: One last minor thing - we also use an internal reranker that is sensitive to token probs; can you recommend calibration for reranker outputs?
[13:28] Leo: We can include reranker specific evals in the pilot; often we keep reranker on FP16 and generator on INT8 to avoid affecting ranking quality.
[13:38] Maya: Awesome. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot planning call and share docs. Thanks everyone.

[13:44] End of meeting notes.
